sections.heading: Is Eightcap Worth Your Money in 2026?
sections.body:
Two hundred and fifty cryptocurrency CFDs under ASIC and FCA regulation. That single fact is why Eightcap exists on every serious crypto trader's shortlist in 2026. While IC Markets offers perhaps 30 coins and Pepperstone a similar count, Eightcap built out an entire crypto ecosystem — from Bitcoin and Ethereum down to altcoins you will not find at any other regulated broker. And they won the 'Best Crypto Broker' award two consecutive years for it.

But strip the crypto away and what remains is still a competent ECN broker. Raw account at 0.0 pips plus $7 round-turn matches Pepperstone and IC Markets exactly — no disadvantage on standard forex pricing. Native TradingView integration means you can execute trades directly from charts without leaving the platform. MT4, MT5, and Capitalise.ai (code-free algo) round out the platform options. No inactivity fee. Free withdrawals.

The 800 total instruments are where Eightcap shows its relative youth. IC Markets has 2,200. Admirals has 8,000. For a pure forex or multi-asset trader, that breadth gap matters. But if crypto CFDs with leverage are your primary trading vehicle — and you want a broker whose regulators would actually respond to a complaint — Eightcap is the answer.

sections.heading: Eightcap Spreads, Fees and Accounts — What Do You Actually Pay in 2026?
sections.body:
Two account types. Raw: 0.0 pips average EUR/USD plus $3.50 per side ($7 round-turn). All-in cost $7 per lot — identical to Pepperstone Razor and IC Markets Raw. Standard: 1.0 pip average EUR/USD, zero commission — all-in approximately $10 per lot. The Raw account is the obvious choice for anyone trading more than casually.

Crypto CFD pricing uses a spread-only model without additional commission. Spreads on BTC/USD are competitive but vary with market conditions — tighter during high-volume hours, wider during quiet periods. The 250+ altcoin selection means you are paying a premium on liquidity for obscure coins, but the access itself is the value proposition.

No inactivity fee — your account stays free regardless of dormancy. No deposit fees. No withdrawal fees. The fee structure is genuinely clean and transparent — what you see is what you pay. No hidden charges surfacing on your statement months later.

sections.heading: Eightcap Final Verdict — Is It Worth It in 2026?
sections.body:
NAFT scores Eightcap 7.6 out of 10. The platform delivers a clear value proposition: the largest regulated crypto CFD selection in the market (250+ coins), native TradingView integration, and Raw ECN pricing that matches the industry's best at $7 round-turn. ASIC, FCA, and CySEC triple-regulation provides Tier-1 oversight with compensation schemes for UK and EU clients. Zero inactivity fees and free withdrawals complete a clean, trader-friendly cost structure.

The limitations are honest: 800 instruments trails the multi-asset leaders. No cTrader. No real stock investing. The 16-year track record is solid but does not carry the same weight as a 25-year veteran. And the 75% UK loss rate — while standard for crypto-heavy CFD providers — reminds you that leverage on volatile assets magnifies losses faster than profits.

NAFT recommends Eightcap for the crypto-focused CFD trader who wants regulation, the TradingView user who wants to trade from charts without compromise, and any trader who values a clean fee structure. If you need 2000+ instruments or cTrader, look at IC Markets. But if crypto CFDs under Tier-1 regulation is your priority, Eightcap has no equal.
